decisions.reason: CH19 lists FATF recommendation categories; CH20 describes World Bank/IMF resources. They share a broad AML/CFT topic but no direct summary, illustration, grounding, or contrast relationship.
Both CPs discuss DNFBP risks (casino junkets vs. real estate/legal), but they merely share the same risk family without a direct review relationship or concrete framework dependency.

CH47 details internal escalation report terminology; CH41 covers the purpose of internal reporting to governance. They share the broad topic of internal reporting but lack a direct structural dependency or summary relationship.
CH41 defines policies vs. procedures; CH51 discusses resource prioritization. They share a broad AFC compliance context but no direct grounding, summary, or illustration link.

CH14 discusses regulatory gaps for DNFBPs; CH12 covers regulatory scrutiny of custodian banks. Both mention regulation but address different sectors and lack a direct structural or review relationship.

CH21 outlines the G-20 ACWG anti-corruption strategies, including 'tackling foreign bribery'; CH02 specializes this by detailing bribery risks and specific anti-bribery controls for financial institutions.
CH26 covers UN ESG initiatives; CH38 covers continuous risk assessment. They share a broad governance/risk context but no direct structural dependency or review relationship.

CH47 defines the Level 2 investigation process and data gathering; CH49 expands this by detailing the specific follow-up risk reassessment and recordkeeping obligations required after such an investigation.

CH20 provides the concrete framework of the OECD Anti-Bribery Convention; CH25 applies this by discussing the extraterritorial reach of specific national ABC frameworks (US, UK, France) that implement such international obligations.
CH41 defines policies vs. procedures; CH49 lists types of law enforcement interactions. They share a broad AFC context but no direct structural dependency or review relationship.
